items.question: Why does the CPU temperature show 0°C?
items.answer: When the CPU temperature shows 0°C, it usually means PawnIO communication was not established correctly. Reinstall the PawnIO components, restart the computer after installation, and then launch THRM again to confirm.

items.question: Which devices are currently supported?
items.answer: Currently supported models include FlyDigi BS1, BS2, BS2PRO, BS3, and BS3PRO.

items.question: What should I do if Bluetooth cannot find the device?
items.answer: If the device does not appear in the Bluetooth scan list, try long-pressing the cooler button to reset Bluetooth advertising. If it still does not recover, contact official support for further assistance.

learning.title: Adaptive learning
learning.description: After longer runtime, the target RPM at each temperature point is fine-tuned automatically so real temperatures stay closer to the configured curve. Learned offsets can be reset at any time.
learning.targetDescription: Adaptive learning tries to settle steady-state temperature near this ceiling. Lower values favor cooling; higher values favor silence.
learning.offsetDescription: The main RPM corrections of the current learned curve relative to the base curve.
learning.noiseTestDescription: Measure real fan noise at each RPM with a microphone. Adaptive learning will then prioritize quiet optimizations where lowering RPM saves the most noise.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Allows learned adjustments above and below the base curve.

cooling.label: Cooling first
cooling.description: Only allows learned RPM increases, avoiding higher idle temperatures.

quiet.label: Quiet first
quiet.description: Only allows learned RPM decreases, avoiding unnecessary fan ramp-up.

learning.predictiveDescription: When CPU/GPU power spikes while temperature is climbing, ramps up against the projected temperature instead of waiting for the measured one to cross the curve point. Ramps up early only, never down; learned offsets still use measured temperatures.
learning.laptopGuardTitle: Ramp down slowly while laptop fans are high
learning.laptopGuardDescription: While the laptop's own fans are still near their recent maximum, the cooling pad drops at most 60 RPM per sampling cycle. That avoids the back-and-forth where a temperature dip cuts pad speed, the temperature bounces back, and it has to ramp up again. Available only on laptops whose fan speed can be read.
learning.laptopGuardToggleAria: Toggle slow ramp-down while laptop fans are high
learning.supersededHint: Adaptive learning 2.0 is on, so these settings are inactive. They are restored untouched when you turn 2.0 off.

noiseTest.title: Fan noise test
noiseTest.description: Measure noise levels at different fan speeds with a microphone and build a noise profile to optimize adaptive learning.

intro.envTitle: Make sure the environment is quiet before testing
intro.point1: Turn off music, videos, air conditioning and other constant sound sources. Do not talk or type during the test.
intro.point2: Place the microphone about 20-30 cm from the cooler and keep it unobstructed.
intro.point3: If you use the laptop's built-in microphone, do not move the device during the test.
intro.point4: Results are relative noise levels (referenced to the quietest step) — no professional acoustic calibration is needed.
intro.sweepNotice: The test sweeps the fan from {{min}} RPM up to {{max}} RPM across {{steps}} measurement points and takes about 2-3 minutes. The fan will get noticeably loud; your previous settings are restored automatically afterwards.

adaptive.title: Adaptive Learning 2.0
adaptive.description: No curve drawing required. It identifies this machine's cooling behaviour online, then generates and keeps refining the whole curve from the preference you set.
adaptive.disabledHint: Once enabled the curve is generated entirely by the algorithm, and curve editing plus adaptive learning 1.0 step aside. Turn it off at any time to get your manual curve back.
adaptive.progressHint: Just use the machine normally under varying loads. Every time the fan holds a stable speed long enough, one sample is recorded; the more it learns, the better the curve fits this machine. Until then it stays close to the conservative built-in curve.
adaptive.limitDescription: A hard constraint independent of preference: reaching this temperature goes to full speed. The floor starts rising gradually from around {{ceiling}}°C rather than jumping at the line.

benefit.title: Cooling Benefit Test
benefit.entryDescription: Measure what this cooler actually buys you at each speed: how many degrees, how many extra watts, and which component benefits most. Independent of learning mode.
benefit.description: Locks the cooler at each speed under one steady workload and samples only after temperatures settle, so the differences can be attributed to the cooler itself.
benefit.intro: The test locks the cooler at {{steps}} speeds in turn, waiting for temperatures to settle before sampling each one — about {{minutes}} minutes in total. Start a sustained, steady workload first (a game, a render, or a stress test) and keep it running unchanged throughout; stopping it partway makes the results meaningless.
benefit.loadReady: Load is ready. You can start.
benefit.loadWaiting: Current power draw is too low. Start a sustained load of at least {{min}}W first, otherwise every fan speed gives the same temperature and nothing can be measured.
benefit.loadLabelDescription: Record what you were running, for later reference. Results from different workloads are not directly comparable.
benefit.settlingHint: Waited {{seconds}}s, temperature spread {{range}}°C. Thermal mass takes time; sampling starts only once the temperature stops drifting.
benefit.samplingHint: Collecting steady-state temperature and power at this speed.
benefit.keepLoadHint: Keep the workload running unchanged — do not close the game or switch away. The fan returns to your previous control mode when the test finishes.

regimeHint.thermal: Temperature is pinned at the limit, so the extra fan speed turns into higher sustained power — the benefit shows up as performance, not as a cooler machine.
regimeHint.power: Power stays constant, so all the extra fan speed turns into lower temperatures — the benefit shows up as temperature and component life.
regimeHint.mixed: Temperature dropped and power rose at the same time: under this workload the cooler makes the machine both cooler and faster.
regimeHint.inconclusive: Neither temperature nor power changed meaningfully. The load may be too light, the machine may not be thermally constrained, or the cooler may not be seated properly.

warnings.loadUnstable: Power draw varied too much between steps, so the workload changed during the test. The temperature differences include load differences and cannot be attributed to the cooler.
warnings.loadTooLight: The load was too light throughout to measure anything. Retest under a sustained heavy load.
warnings.notSettled: Some steps were still drifting when sampled, so those readings are off their true steady-state values.
warnings.rpmUnreachable: The fan could not reach some target speeds, so the high-speed steps were not actually measured.
warnings.fewSteps: Too few valid steps to show a trend.

benefit.sensorsDescription: Change from the lowest to the highest speed. A whole-machine average would flatten a 12°C GPU hot-spot drop and a 2°C CPU drop into one meaningless number, so each is listed separately. Click any row to plot it in the temperature chart above.

errors.idle: Current draw is only {{watts}}W, below {{min}}W. Start a sustained load before running the test.

flydigi.title: Flydigi Space Station compatibility
flydigi.description: Stop the Flydigi background service from taking over the cooler
flydigi.tip: The Flydigi Space Station service runs as SYSTEM and keeps pushing fan and lighting commands to the cooler, fighting THRM for control. When enabled, THRM writes a security descriptor on the cooler device that only allows the current user, locking that service out. Flydigi's controller mapping, virtual keyboard/mouse and trigger features are unaffected. Requires administrator rights; turning it off restores everything.
